html:
The Caracazo was a wave of riots and looting in Caracas and other cities that began on 27 February 1989, set off by a sharp rise in bus fares. Security forces killed hundreds of people, possibly many more, in the days that followed.

President Carlos Andrés Pérez had just begun reforms backed by the International Monetary Fund, raising petrol prices after years of debt and falling oil income. Poor people from the hillside barrios came down into the city. The government declared a state of emergency and sent in the army, which fired on crowds and into homes.

The Caracazo shattered faith in the parties that had ruled since 1958 under the pact of Betancourt. Three years later the army officer Hugo Chávez led a failed coup in its name. It is the turning point of modern Venezuela, in the city of Caracas.
